newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf oil exploration boosts local shipping.
newsitem.headline: Gulf oil exploration boosts local shipping.

text.p: Strong oil exploration activity in the Gulf has led to higher contract rates for ships which service the industry, Gulf shipping firms said on Wednesday.
General supply, utility and crew ships as well as tug and piloting boats were in heavy demand from state and international oil firms carrying out drilling and development work, they said.
"The market on the marine side is extremely buoyant...We have 100 percent utilisation at the moment because of an extremely high level of drilling," said one shipping manager.
One major shipping line in Dubai quoted rates of around $5,500-$6,000 a day for a standard support vessel under a long-term contract versus $3,500 compared to a year ago.
Prices have been depressed for most of this decade and rates were now approaching a level when shipowners were prepared to consider building new capacity.

Higher shipping costs were mainly led by demand from Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Oman and Saudi Arabia for boats able to supply everything from crew, supplies, drilling fluids to transporting rigs, shippers said.
Daily drilling rig rates have doubled in less than 18 months to their highest levels in 15 years because of tight availability following accelerated oil and gas exploration programmes in Gulf states.
OPEC member Qatar has launched an aggressive oil and gas development programme with the help of foreign firms in a move to develop its massive gas deposits at the offshore North Field.
International firms are also carrying out major exploration and development work at Qatar's offshore oilfields.
Higher exploration activity has been prompted in the Gulf by a general uptrend in oil prices since 1994.
